page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.large is a burstable, shared-core virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing two virtual CPUs mapped to a single physical core via hyperthreading. Memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB total, delivering 4.0 GB per virtual CPU. The instance provides no bundled local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and includes no dedicated hardware GPUs. Network baseline bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark results reflect the shared and burstable resource allocation of the underlying hardware. Single-core stress-ng scores reach 1161.28 and multi-core scores reach 2371.48, placing CPU processing in the bottom quartile of evaluated cloud instances. Geekbench results confirm this baseline, with a single-core score of 1092.0 and a multi-core score of 1822.0. Memory throughput yields 22.38 GB/sec read and 19.14 GB/sec write on large blocks. Application benchmarks show 2.61 million Redis SET operations per second, 2.58 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and 43.21 tokens per second text generation on a 135M small language model.

The primary operational tradeoff of the ecs.t6-c1m4.large is its burstable CPU model and shared hardware tenancy, which can result in variable performance under sustained utilization. However, its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides sufficient RAM for low-intensity applications without requiring overprovisioned compute. The instance is suited for non-critical development and test environments, small staging servers, lightweight internal tools, low-traffic web applications, and background administrative jobs with intermittent activity.

The configuration features no local storage or GPU hardware, and operates with a 0 Gbps baseline network profile. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves 1161.28 in stress-ng single-core compute, 1822.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, and 2.61 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory bandwidth yields 22.38 GB/sec on uncached reads. Due to its burstable allocation and shared infrastructure, the instance provides cost-conscious capacity for development servers, low-concurrency web serving, and lightweight background automation tasks.
